# [repair] Leaf spring and shackle repair

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Secure rear truck, remove sway bar and U-bolts, then jack axle away from springs to insert Add-A-Leaf. [t932]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Secure the rear truck on jack stands, placing them slightly in front of the leaf spring mounts.
2. [Partial] Remove the sway bar and lower strut bolts to let the axle hang loosely.
3. [Partial] Clamp both sides of the leaf springs together at outer edges using four clamps for stability during reassembly.
4. Unbolt the U-bolts holding the axel on both sides of the spring pack.
5. [Partial] Jack up the entire rear axle assembly away from the springs, watching closely to avoid pinching brake or ABS lines.
6. Use vice grips to hold the top of an old spring bolt while using an impact wrench to remove the nut.
7. [Partial] Compress the leaf packs with a 6-inch C-clamp on the center AAL bolts before inserting them into the pack.

_Procedure reported by [t932]._

## Tools

- Jack stands (extra set recommended) [t932]

## Parts

- Center C-brackets [t932]
- [Partial] DEAVER Add-A-Leaf, AAL [t932]
- U-bolts [t932]

## Tips & gotchas

- Orient the AAL bolt so the longer side faces forward and aligns with the leaf pack. [t932]
- Use a 6-inch C-clamp to compress leaves before tightening center bolts for easier installation. [t932]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Over-tightening the center nut which can strip the threads on the AAL bolt. [t932]
